evidence: Workbook check 1: 'The prompt reads like a real person asking for an app, not a spec sheet, checklist, or build recipe.' Skill quality-checks.md check 1 defines the defect as 'numbered acceptance lists, a "shall/must" spec table, a feature matrix, or a build recipe (framework, file layout, endpoint list) instead of a product ask.' task/instruction.md is three short first-person prose paragraphs with none of these. Line 1 states a product ask with a personal use case: 'I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files. The editor itself matters: I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source. I want to keep the versions that work without losing a draft when another tab saves first.' Line 3 points at the supporting material rather than restating it: 'Please read the six notes in /instructions before building.' (six notes exist: behaviour, integration, overview, policy, security, ui). Line 5 gives only the delivery location and an outcome: 'Put the app in /app and serve the workspace at /. I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in.' There are no numbered or bulleted lists, no tables, no 'must'/'shall', no framework mandate, no file layout and no endpoint list in instruction.md; '/app' and '/' are the only build-facing details. The template instruction.md is a CHANGE_ME placeholder, so no template-controlled wording was required or altered. Scope of this verdict is instruction.md only (block A, row 1); the six notes carry the detailed behaviour and launch contract (for example integration.md names port 3000, node /app/server.js and GET /api/health) and are for other rows to judge. Observation, not a defect for this row: '/assets/seed_data.json describes the starting scope' is slightly stiff phrasing for a seed whose content is an empty snippet list plus a one-line note; it still reads as a person pointing at a file.
